Subject: Compute slate orchestration & deal-linked capacity plan — NovusAI

Hi Emma —

Quick follow to our demo last week. We sketched a few potential commitment shapes for the Dedicated offering and I put together a working proposal that ties the GPU slate to the commercial milestones you shared (growth to 3M monthly requests / model mix change in Q4).

The attachment "NovusAI_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.xlsx" contains three lanes: Anchor (50 A100-equivalent), Growth (120), and Burst (200 capped). Key pieces to note:
- Minimum guaranteed: 25 GPUs for 6 months (soft start month-to-month after month 6)
- Ramp schedule: 25 -> 50 in month 1-2, -> 100 by month 6, reserve review at month 9
- Canary policy: start 5 GPUs for pre-prod and 10 for canary evaluation before full activation

Two asks from your side for the next iteration:
1) Confirm which model families will be primary in months 1 and 6 (we need seq length and KV cache sizing)
2) Identify any hard procurement windows for budget sign-off (Doc says target by 05/10)

I included Karthik and Monica to help scope the technical onboarding and billing cadence. If agreeable, we can convert the workbook to a redlined commitment PDF and route through legal.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0184

Attachment: NovusAI_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12 sheets)

Thanks David — this looks helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- Model roadmap: months 1–3 will primarily run the t-encoder family (shorter seqs), months 4+ we expect to add g-family (longer seqs for document understanding).
- Procurement timeline: finance has a budget approval meeting 05/05; if we can get an updated PDF by 04/22 that shows monthly cost cadence that will help.
- SLA ask: we need a 99.5% uptime SLA on the Anchor lane during business hours. Can you confirm if that is feasible for the 50-GPU configuration?

Also looping in a question from ops — do you support a geo-burst option (US-West primary, US-East warm standby) for cross-region failover?

Best,
Emma Walsh
Head of Platform — NovusAI
emma.walsh@novusai.com

Subject: Re: Compute slate orchestration & deal-linked capacity plan — NovusAI

Emma —

Short answers from a technical/ops standpoint:
- 99.5% during business hours: we can commit to that on the Anchor lane assuming the reserved pool of 50 GPUs and standard redundancy (N+1 for host failures). We will include an explicit SLA clause in the next PDF.
- Geo-burst: supported. Proposed pattern: US-West primary, US-East warm standby with warm/km cache migration. Warm standby cost is ~20% of active capacity; we can show cost delta in the updated workbook.
- Sequence length planning: for t-encoders we recommend a 2x KV cache per GPU baseline; for g-family longer sequences we recommend reserving 1.8x additional memory capacity per GPU or opting to move some traffic to a larger-VM SKU (we show an example in the timeline).

A few operational notes we recommend adding to the proposal:
1) Pre-prod canary window (2 weeks) on 5 GPUs to validate model perf and token budgeting.
2) Autoscale burst gates for live seasonality (up to burst cap) with a 10-minute cooldown.
3) Monthly checkpoint review with your ML infra team to adjust quantization and batching knobs if we observe tail latency regressions.

I'll hand off to Monica for the onboarding calendar and billing cadence details.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Compute slate orchestration & deal-linked capacity plan — NovusAI

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the quick confirmation on model families and the procurement window. Per David/Karthik notes, attached is a follow-up timeline "SLA_Ramp_Timeline.pdf" that maps the ramp to milestone gates and billing triggers. Highlights: 

- Activation week 0–2: Provision 25 GPUs, run pre-prod canary (5 GPUs) and production warmup for 10% of traffic.
- Month 1–2: Move to Anchor lane (50 GPUs) once canary passes and procurement signature is received. Billing starts pro-rata from activation date.
- Month 3–6: Growth lane phased expansion to 100 GPUs if traffic >= 1.5M req/day for 14 consecutive days; automatic autoscale to Burst lane (up to 200 GPUs) for traffic spikes, subject to usage-based overage pricing.
- Review & renew: Formal capacity review at month 6 and 9; changes to min GPUs require 30 days notice prior to the month boundary.

Other contract mechanics we included in the attached timeline/workbook:
- Warm standby charge (US-East) at 20% of provisioned active Anchor pool cost.
- Canary credit: 2 weeks free warmup credit if canary performance meets latency and token-cost targets.
- Early decommit: 3-month termination notice for mid-term decommit with pro-rated refund schedule.

Next steps:
1) David — share a redlined PDF for procurement by 04/22 (Emma needed the monthly cost cadence).
2) Emma/procurement — confirm the signatory and any PO requirements.
3) Karthik/Monica — schedule a 60-minute onboarding planning call (ops, security, ML infra) the week of 04/26.

I'll update the HubSpot deal with the attachments and timeline link.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Onboarding Lead — Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: SLA_Ramp_Timeline.pdf (3 pages)
